data.title: Gold, silver ETFs gain up to 4% on rebound in precious metals
data.description:
Gold, silver ETFs gain up to 4%.

Gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) gained up to 4 per cent on Friday, tracking a recovery in precious metal prices in the domestic and international markets.Silver ETFs led the gains, with Nippon India Silver ETF rising 4.25 per cent, Tata Silver ETF gaining 4.14 per cent and ICICI Prudential Silver ETF advancing 4 per cent.Gold ETFs also traded higher, with ICICI Prudential Gold ETF gaining 2.87 per cent, Nippon India ETF Gold BeES rising 2.79 per cent, SBI Gold ETF advancing 2.8 per cent and Tata Gold ETF gaining 2.7 per cent.The gains came after a recent sharp correction in precious metal ETFs, following a decline in international gold and silver prices from elevated levels.In the international market, silver futures rose 6.15 per cent to USD 44.10 per ounce. Spot gold gained 2.9 per cent to USD 3,670.69 per ounce, recovering after touching its lowest level since August 2025 on Wednesday. US gold futures for December delivery advanced 3.9 per cent to USD 3,669.30 per ounce.On the domestic front, silver prices rose 5.1 per cent to Rs 1,53,277 per kg in futures trade on Friday, tracking firm global trends.On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), silver contracts for December delivery gained Rs 7,434, or 5.1 per cent, to Rs 1,53,277 per kg. The contract recorded a business turnover of 4,050 lots.Fresh positions built by participants supported the rise in silver prices, analysts said.Jateen Trivedi, Vice President, Research Analyst – Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities, said gold witnessed strong short covering, gaining around Rs 3,150, or 2.6 per cent, to trade near Rs 1,25,500."With COMEX prices moving decisively above the USD 3,650 mark, the next resistance is placed around USD 3,675-3,700, where further profit booking cannot be ruled out," he said.Trivedi added that volatility could remain elevated next week amid several key US economic data releases and policy-related events.On the domestic front, gold is expected to trade in the range of Rs 1,22,000-Rs 1,28,500, and traders should maintain disciplined risk management amid sharp price movements, he said.

Shares of Gokaldas Exports, Sportking India, and other textile companies rose up to 8% as a report said global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs, including India, in the first half of November.

Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs, including India, in the first half of November, three factory owners told Reuters.

The factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world's second-largest apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing, Reuters reported.

Gokaldas Exports and Sporking are suppliers for H&M and ZARA, whose shares rose 8% each on November 27.

Related Stories

  • Textile stocks: Gokaldas Exports, Arvind, Kitex Garments fall as proposed US tariffs raise export co...
  • Gokaldas Exports Q2 results: Net profit soars 410% YoY to Rs 41 crore
  • Gokaldas Exports Q2 consolidated PAT jumps to Rs 41 crore

Other textile companies' stocks like Vardhman Textiles, Trident rose 2.4% and 3.9%, respectively.

India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the order diversions, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.

Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, though the rise was the smallest in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers' demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was "satisfactory" and that he hoped all garment workers would resume work from Saturday.

M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, told Reuters that higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers.

"The wage increase has added to costs at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying," he said.

India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.

Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added.

data.title: SEBI may revisit Rs 2 lakh retail investor limit in IPOs if warranted; ICDR working group may examine issue
data.description:
• SEBI may review the Rs 2 lakh retail IPO limit.
  • Retail investors typically apply for just one lot.
  • A working group is set up to review regulations.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) may examine whether the Rs 2 lakh threshold for retail investors in initial public offerings (IPOs) needs to be revised as part of a broader review of issuance regulations, a senior official said.

The Rs 2 lakh limit has remained unchanged for more than 25 years, but the regulator has so far seen little merit in revising it, given that retail investors typically apply for a single lot in an IPO, which often costs around Rs 15,000, said Jeevan Sonparote, Executive Director, SEBI.

Speaking at Moneycontrol FiDEX 2.0 in Mumbai, Sonparote said that even if the retail investor threshold were raised to Rs 5 lakh, it may not materially change the amount investors apply for in an IPO.

“The limit of Rs 2 lakh has been a very old limit. It's more than 25 years now. This limit has not been reviewed. There were various attempts made earlier to review this particular limit,” Sonparote said.

However, he said the regulator had found little justification for revising the threshold, as retail investors typically apply for one lot in an IPO, which may cost around Rs 15,000.

Related Stories

  • SEBI summons APL Apollo officials over Tata Steel deal, examines possible RPT rule violations
  • SEBI bars Le Lavoir, chairman and 13 others over alleged price manipulation, fund diversion, action ...
  • APL Apollo’s minority shareholders will 'foot the bill' in Tata Steel deal: IiAS suggests Sebi sho...

“So, even if today if somebody says that I want to invest in a retail category, he is doing only one lot and one lot may not be more than Rs 15,000. So, even if I were to increase this to, let's say, Rs 5 lakh, a retail investor will continue to apply at Rs 15,000,” he said.

Also read: Grey market premium is akin to betting, SEBI seeks to choke revenue incentives for such platforms

Sonparote said the treatment of investors during the allotment process would also remain unchanged, irrespective of whether the threshold was increased.

“There appears to be no such reason to review the limit. However, if there is some such thought process, we should definitely look at it,” he said.

SEBI has already constituted a working group to review the issuance regulations, and the retail investor threshold could be among the issues taken up by the panel, Sonparote said.

“I think you'll be aware that SEBI has already set up a working group on the review of the issuance regulations. One of the issues would definitely be whether to review this particular limit. That should be one of the issues that the committee or working group should visit,” he said.

Also read: SEBI may ease SIF norms further, consider giving fund managers more flexibility 

In October 2010, SEBI, under the chairmanship of CB Bhave, doubled the retail investor limit for IPO applications to Rs 2 lakh from the earlier cap of Rs 1 lakh, which had been in force since March 2005.

The issue has been raised several times by various stakeholders since then, but SEBI has held back from changing the limit, as IPO application data did not support the proposal.

US stock futures rallied sharply on Friday, signalling a strong opening for Wall Street as trading resumes after the Thanksgiving holiday, with renewed investor appetite for beaten-down artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. The gains come towards the end of a volatile week that saw dramatic swings in technology stocks amid persistent concerns over AI investments and elevated valuations.

Nasdaq 100 futures surged 729 points, or 2.8 percent, to 26,829.3, while S&P 500 futures advanced 144.8 points, or 2 percent, to 7,340.5. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gained 672 points, or 1.3 percent, to 50,900.

The rally in US stock futures gathered momentum during Asian trading, building on Wednesday's late-session recovery on Wall Street ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

AI stocks set for recovery after volatile week

US technology stocks have witnessed sharp swings this week as investors weigh increasingly attractive valuations following the recent correction against persistent concerns over the massive capital expenditure undertaken by AI companies and the potential returns on these investments.

Related Stories

  • GIFT Nifty mildly up, US futures ease as Nvidia rally cools; Asian stocks surge

Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive triggered a spectacular rally on Monday, with the chipmaker's shares surging 31.5 percent and restoring nearly $1 trillion in market capitalisation. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.5 percent, while the S&P 500 gained 4.7 percent.

However, the recovery lost momentum over the following two sessions. Nvidia shares fell 5.9 percent on Tuesday and another 3.9 percent on Wednesday, while shares of Anthropic slipped below their IPO price of $83 apiece, less than a week after the Claude developer's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.

The Nasdaq Composite plunged more than 4 percent during Wednesday's session before recovering much of its losses to close 0.6 percent lower. The S&P 500 declined 0.3 percent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.3 percent.

Asian markets extend gains

The renewed appetite for technology stocks was also reflected in Asian equity markets, with the MSCI Asia Pacific Index advancing 1.8 percent on Friday. South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix was among the stocks leading the regional recovery for a second consecutive session.

Asian technology stocks have been particularly hard hit by the recent unwinding of the global AI trade, with semiconductor-heavy markets such as South Korea and Taiwan suffering steep losses this month.

US Fed rate hike expectations remain elevated; Brent nears $98

Despite the recovery in equities, expectations of further monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve remain firmly entrenched. Traders are pricing in a 99 percent probability of an interest rate increase at the US Fed's December meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch, Reuters reported.

Meanwhile, international crude oil prices reversed their morning losses amid persistent concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East. Brent crude advanced 1.3 percent to $97.8 a barrel, adding to its sharp gains this week.

data.title: SEBI summons APL Apollo officials over Tata Steel deal, examines possible RPT rule violations
data.description:
SEBI summons APL Apollo officials over Tata Steel deal, examines possible RPT rule violations: Sources
  • SEBI examines APL Apollo and Tata Steel deal structure.
  • Regulator checks for potential related-party rule dodging.
  • Proxy firms flag governance concerns over the transaction.
Did our AI summary help?

Market Mastery

Webinar by Vishal Malkan

Find the weak links

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Noticing the concerns of moinority shareholders market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has summoned key officials of APL Apollo Tubes to explain the structure of its proposed transactions with Tata Steel, as the market regulator examines whether the arrangement violates related-party transaction (RPT) norms, sources familiar with the development told Moneycontrol. The regulator may next call the officials of Tata Steel also to explain the deal.

SEBI is examining whether a series of interconnected transactions between the two companies and entities associated with APL Apollo's outgoing promoters should be treated as related-party transactions, despite being structured and announced in stages.

“If the regulator finds that the arrangement was designed to circumvent RPT requirements, it could direct the companies to seek the shareholders' approval” as applicable for RPTs", a source on the conditions of anonymity said.

The scrutiny raises wider corporate governance questions over whether companies can structure a composite business arrangement as separate transactions to avoid regulatory requirements intended to protect minority shareholders.

For the protection of minority shareholders interest, under listing regulations (LODR Regulations), SEBI and exchanges can apply the purpose-and-effect test, to examine whether a transaction, irrespective of its legal form or timing, is structured to achieve an outcome that would otherwise attract related-party transaction (RPT) norms.

Related Stories

  • APL Apollo Tubes shares rise 3.5% after 30% rout; Tata Steel weighs options to address investor conc...
  • SEBI bars Le Lavoir, chairman and 13 others over alleged price manipulation, fund diversion, action ...
  • APL Apollo’s minority shareholders will 'foot the bill' in Tata Steel deal: IiAS suggests Sebi sho...

Another person familiar with the issue said, “SEBI can look beyond individual agreements and assess interconnected transactions collectively to determine whether they effectively constitute an RPT”.

Also read: SEBI bars Le Lavoir, chairman and 13 others over alleged price manipulation, fund diversion, action before lock in expiry

In the Tata Steel–APL Apollo case, the key question is whether the business transfers were agreed just before Tata Steel acquired control to avoid mandatory minority shareholder approval under Regulation 23 of listing regulations. All material related party transactions and subsequent material modifications require prior shareholder approval, in which promoters are restricted from voting.

Materiality threshold is linked to annual consolidated turnover. It is 10 percent for companies with turnover up to Rs 20,000 crore; Rs 2,000 crore plus 5 percent of the excess turnover for those between Rs 20,000 crore and Rs 40,000 crore; and Rs 3,000 crore plus 2.5 percent of excess turnover above Rs 40,000 crore, capped at Rs 5,000 cror

The key issues

The controversy centres on Tata Steel's proposed purchase of APL Apollo's Steel Tubes and Colour Coated businesses. Under the proposed deal, Tata Steel will sell its Steel Tubes business, valued at Rs 11,700 crore, and Tata Steel Colors Private Limited, valued at Rs 16,300 crore, to APL Apollo for a total consideration of Rs 28,000 crore.

Tata Steel holds 50 percent in Tata Steel Colors directly and the remaining 50 percent through its wholly owned subsidiary, Tata Steel Downstream Products Limited. Another issue is its acquisition of the promoter stake in APL Apollo and a proposed manufacturing arrangement involving SG Tech Engineering, an entity associated with the outgoing promoter group.

 Proxy advisory firms flag governance concerns

Proxy advisory firms have raised corporate governance and minority shareholder concerns over the Tata Steel–APL Apollo deal, questioning whether its four interconnected transactions should be examined collectively by SEBI.

SES alleged that the structure may have been designed to keep the asset transfers outside the related-party transaction (RPT) framework. It questioned the sequencing of business transfer agreements on November 22 and Tata Steel’s acquisition of a 9.91 percent stake in APL Apollo a day later, besides flagging potential promoter conflicts of interest.

“Finding a way out and ensuring a law is not applicable is an art, unfortunately while art of Picasso may be appreciated by all, however, art of dodging law is not appreciated by investors,” SES said, adding that share prices of both companies reflected investor dissatisfaction.

IiAS said, “The deal makes commercial sense... Where the parties went wrong was in presenting a single deal as several separate transactions.” It urged SEBI to examine differential treatment and the risk of minority shareholders bearing acquisition debt without RPT safeguards.

InGovern called for a substance-over-form review, independent fairness opinion, transparent disclosures and shareholder approval. “The central issue is whether the transaction, viewed in its commercial substance, was structured to benefit APL Apollo’s promoter group,” it said.

It warned that shareholders who do not tender in the Rs 2,301.40 open offer would remain exposed to acquisition debt, integration and valuation risks, and related-party arrangements.

The concerns have gained significance as investors in both Tata Steel and APL Apollo have expressed dissatisfaction with the deal.

An email sent to SEBI and APL Apollo Tubes did not elicit any response, before publishing the story.

The system combines a 64-tube air defence rocket launcher (Version-I) with a 64-micro-missile launcher (Version-II), featuring autonomous guidance and infrared seekers to engage multiple drones.

During an earnings call, the company said it expects to complete its internal trials and conduct field trials within the current calendar year, following which commercialisation would begin.

"There is a huge demand for such kind of products," the company said.

Meanwhile, Paras Defence and Space Technologies, Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL) and Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) gained between 3 percent and 6 percent.

HAL shares advanced after brokerage firm Elara Capital maintained its 'Buy' rating on the stock and raised its target price to Rs 6,270 from Rs 6,000. The revised target indicates an upside potential of nearly 28 percent from the stock's previous closing price.

Meanwhile, shares of Omnitech Engineering rallied as much as 5 percent after the company announced it received a development order from BrahMos Aerospace for assemblies and sub-assemblies of metallic airframe components and canister subsystems.

Harshit Kapadia, Vice President - Industrial, Defence, Railway, Consumer Electrical/Durables/Electronics at Elara Securities told CNBC-TV18, that the Ministry of Defence's Rs 1,980-crore agreement linked to Israel's Barak air defence system may lead to a large part of the programme to be indigenised, with Bharat Electronics and Bharat Dynamics likely to benefit from domestic manufacturing and missile production.
